## 1

I’m really sorry—it sounds like you’ve been carrying this for a long time. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk through what’s been happening? If the workplace is unsafe or seriously harming your health, you don’t have to endure it, but it may help to make a plan first: check your finances, review notice requirements, and look into other options. I’m here to listen, and you don’t have to figure it out alone tonight.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem questionable, especially when they’re edited, compressed, or presented without context. But the evidence that Earth is spherical doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing over the horizon from the bottom up, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, see different stars from different latitudes, and track satellites and spacecraft ourselves. Independent space agencies, universities, companies, and amateur observers all obtain consistent results. Faking all of that evidence across countries and decades would be far more complicated than the straightforward explanation: Earth is round.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors—like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more easily than red or orange light, so blue light spreads across the sky and reaches our eyes from all around us.

At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere. A lot of the blue light gets scattered away before the sunlight reaches us, leaving more reds, oranges, and pinks. That’s why the sky can look so different at different times of day.
